To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a multitask learning architecture for semantic localization and odometry, we propose an adaptive weighted fusion layer that aggregates temporal information and fuses semantic features, we introduce a self supervised warpping technique for learning consistent semantics and we introduce a first urban outdoor localization dataset for training deep networks.

1) multitask learning can be successfully applied to the problem of semantic localization, 2) semantic understanding can be exploited to improve localization performance, 3) the proposed self supervised warping scheme improves the semantic understanding of the network, 4) a novel fusion layer can be used to aggregate temporal information for improving the localization accuracy, and 5) our approach is robust in challenging scenarios.

we propose the first deep multitask learning framework that simultaneously solves semantic understanding, localization and odometry, and that our approach outperforms local feature based methods on the challenging 7 Scenes benchmark.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of simultaneous semantic scene understanding and state estimation.
the development and analysis of deep learning based methods for simultaneous semantic understanding and visual localization in urban environments.

the following: (i) the design of a multitask learning architecture that enables deep networks to encode scene specific constraints for the benefit of localization; (ii) the development of a self supervised war ping technique that exploits relative motion to learn consistent semantic features; (iii) the design of an adaptive fusion layer that aggregates motion specific temporal information for the localization stream; (iv) the development of the first urban outdoor localization dataset for training deep networks; (v) the design of the VLocNet architecture
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our work is the first to demonstrate that semantic understanding can benefit localization and odometry tasks, and that localization and odometry can benefit semantic understanding tasks, and that this mutual benefit is substantial.
the proposed method outperforms the state of the arts by a large margin and that the method is able to perform semantic localization and odometry in challenging scenarios.
the VLocNet architecture is the best performing approach on the 7Scenes benchmark, and the best multitask approach on the DeepLoc dataset.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel deep network for joint semantic understanding and localization that exploits the inter task relationship to learn consistent semantics and robust global localization.
we have demonstrated a new way to combine localization with semantic understanding, which we believe will be an important step forward in the field of robot autonomy.
VLocNet+ is a deep multitask network for semantic understanding and state estimation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the interdependence between scene understanding and localization tasks can be exploited for improving each of these tasks, and the proposed approach is a promising step towards achieving a fully integrated semantic understanding and localization system.
multitask learning can help to improve the performance of localization by incorporating semantic understanding of the scene and that this can be achieved by a single deep network.
the proposed multitask learning approach can enable a wide range of scene understanding tasks to be tackled jointly and simultaneously.
